what.definition: Four Element Monk is a Baldur's Gate 3 build that combines Monk martial abilities with elemental spellcasting from all four schools: Fire, Cold, Lightning, and Acid.
what.summary: Comprehensive build guide for the Monk of the Four Elements, covering subclass features, spell selection, Ki point optimization, and multiclass synergy with Sorcerer metamagic.
bullets: Elemental Attunement grants free cantrips at all four elements
Twin Elemental Wrath infuses unarmed strikes with dual-element damage
Four Point Attack unleashes four elemental strikes per turn
Strix Cove Monk Cloak enables out-of-combat casting and saves a Quiver slot
Sorcerer multiclass unlocks Twinned Spell for double-target magic

why.summary: Pure monks struggle with AoE and range. Pure spellcasters lack survivability. Four Element Monk bridges both, delivering burst elemental damage with monk mobility and defense.
why.impact: Twin Elemental Wrath and Four Point Attack create unmatched single-target and AoE flexibility, while Empty Body provides invulnerability and mist form for clutch moments.

terms.shortDefinition: Resource pool spent on monk abilities and elemental spellcasting.
terms.detailedDefinition: Ki Points are the core resource for Four Element Monk. They scale with Monk level (starting at 2 at level 2, reaching 5 at level 13). Elemental spells cost Ki to cast, Twin Elemental Wrath costs 1 Ki, and Four Point Attack costs 4 Ki. Ki refreshes on a Short Rest.
terms.whyItMatters: Every aspect of the build revolves around Ki economy. Managing Ki spending between combat rounds determines your damage output and survivability.

dialogue.user: How many Ki do I get?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Ki scales with Monk level: 2 at lvl 2, 3 at lvl 5, 4 at lvl 11, 5 at lvl 13. All refresh on Short Rest.

terms.shortDefinition: Gain cantrips from all four elemental schools.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 3, you gain access to one cantrip from each elemental school: Fire (Produce Flame), Cold (Ray of Frost), Lightning (Shocking Grasp), and Acid (Acid Splash). At Monk 11, you can change these cantrips on a Long Rest.
terms.whyItMatters: Your baseline damage options. Acid Splash is especially valuable since it hits multiple targets.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Produce Flame, Ray of Frost, Shocking Grasp, and Acid Splash. Swap on Long Rest at Monk 11+.

terms.shortDefinition: Infuse unarmed strikes with two elemental damages for 1 Ki.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 3, spend 1 Ki to attune two unarmed strikes with elemental damage. Choose two elements from Fire, Cold, Lightning, or Acid. Each attuned strike deals 1d6 of the chosen elemental damage on top of your normal unarmed strike damage. Attunements last until end of next turn.
terms.whyItMatters: Your most-used combat ability. Consistent elemental damage on every attack, triggering elemental resistances and vulnerabilities.

dialogue.user: Should I use Twin Elemental Wrath every fight?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Yes — 1 Ki for two 1d6-infused strikes is excellent value. Pair with high-Dexterity builds for maximum hit rate.

terms.shortDefinition: Make four unarmed strikes, each infused with a different element for 4 Ki.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 11, spend 4 Ki to make four unarmed strikes. Each strike is automatically attuned to a different element (one Fire, one Cold, one Lightning, one Acid), dealing 1d6 extra elemental damage per strike. Cannot miss — each strike automatically hits a target within reach.
terms.whyItMatters: Your ultimate nuke. Bypasses resistance splitting and guarantees four elemental hits. Devastating against single targets or groups.

dialogue.user: Is Four Point Attack worth 4 Ki?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Four guaranteed hits with different elements — it shredssingle targets and ignores resistance. Best saved for bosses.

terms.shortDefinition: Cast elemental spells without spending Ki points.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 15, your elemental spells no longer consume Ki points. You can still spend Ki to cast them at a higher level, but the base cast is free. This transforms your Ki economy dramatically.
terms.whyItMatters: Game-changing at level 15. You can spam Conjure Flame, Ice Knife, and Call Lightning without touching your Ki pool.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Elemental Mastery makes your spells free to cast. Save Ki for Twin Elemental Wrath and Four Point Attack.

terms.shortDefinition: Spend Ki to temporarily boost AC.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 7, spend Ki points to increase your AC. Each Ki point spent adds +1 to your AC until the start of your next turn. This stacks with your existing Dexterity-based AC calculation.
terms.whyItMatters: Critical survivability tool. Spending 2-3 Ki can raise your AC to 20+, making you nearly unhittable for a round.

dialogue.user: How do I survive boss fights?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Flowing Barrier + Patient Defense + high Dexterity. Stack to AC 20+ and use Step of the Wind to reposition.

terms.shortDefinition: Cast Mirror Image and Teleport without spell slots.
terms.detailedDefinition: At Monk 14, you can spend 4 Ki to cast Mirror Image or Teleport at will. These spells don't consume spell slots since they're monk abilities, not spellcasting.
terms.whyItMatters: Teleport is invaluable for repositioning, escaping grapple ranges, and flanking. Mirror Image provides massive AC soft cap.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Yes — Empty Body lets you Teleport for 4 Ki. Use it to flank, escape, or reposition for Four Point Attack.

terms.shortDefinition: Legendary cloak granting monk features and out-of-combat spellcasting.
terms.detailedDefinition: A legendary item found in Act 3 that grants access to monk features and lets Four Element Monk cast spells outside of combat. Normally, monks can only cast elemental spells during combat. This cloak removes that restriction and saves an equipment Quiver slot.
terms.whyItMatters: Best-in-slot item for this build. Enables exploration utility from spells like Conjure Flame for light and Ice Knife for crowd control outside combat.

dialogue.user: Can I cast spells outside combat?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Only with the Strix Cove Monk Cloak from Act 3. It's mandatory for full build flexibility.

terms.shortDefinition: Legendary gauntlets that boost damage when Ki is spent.
terms.detailedDefinition: Legendary gauntlets found in Act 2 that increase unarmed strike damage and gain additional effects when Ki abilities are used. Synergizes perfectly with Four Element Monk's Ki-heavy playstyle.
terms.whyItMatters: Massive damage multiplier for unarmed strikes. Combined with Twin Elemental Wrath, each hit deals significantly more damage.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Patient-0 gauntlets are best-in-slot. They amplify unarmed strike damage and trigger on Ki abilities.

terms.shortDefinition: Take Sorcerer levels for Metamagic and spell slot flexibility.
terms.detailedDefinition: Dipping into Sorcerer (typically 2-4 levels) grants Metamagic Adept feat-equivalent abilities. Twinned Spell lets you target two enemies with single-target spells. Quickened Spell allows casting a spell and attacking in the same turn.
terms.whyItMatters: Twinned Spell with Conjure Flame or Ice Knife doubles your AoE potential. Sorcerer spell slots supplement monk casting.

dialogue.aiQuestion: Sorcerer 2-4 is the optimal dip. Twinned Spell alone transforms single-target spells into dual-target nukes.

terms.shortDefinition: Rare gloves that add elemental damage to unarmed strikes.
terms.detailedDefinition: Rare gauntlets that add elemental damage to unarmed strikes. Synergizes with Twin Elemental Wrath by adding an additional layer of elemental damage on top of the monk's infused strikes.
terms.whyItMatters: Stacks with Twin Elemental Wrath for triple-layered elemental damage on unarmed strikes.

dialogue.user: What gloves stack with Twin Elemental Wrath?
dialogue.aiQuestion: Dragon's Claw Gloves add elemental damage that stacks with your monk infusion.

terms.shortDefinition: Spellcasting staff boosting spell damage and granting spell attacks.
terms.detailedDefinition: A powerful spellcasting staff that enhances spell attack rolls and damage. Provides spellcasting stat bonuses and additional spell effects that complement the Four Element Monk's spell-heavy gameplay.
terms.whyItMatters: Boosts spell attack rolls and damage for your elemental spells, increasing both hit rate and damage output.

dialogue.aiQuestion: A spellcasting staff boosts your spell attacks. The Staff of the Woodland Romance is a strong option in Act 2.

categories.title: Elemental Attunement
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 3
categories.description: Gain one cantrip from each elemental school: Fire, Cold, Lightning, and Acid.
categories.details: Starting cantrips: Produce Flame (Fire), Ray of Frost (Cold), Shocking Grasp (Lightning), Acid Splash (Acid). At Monk 11, you can change each cantrip to another option from the same school on a Long Rest. Cantrips scale with character level, not Monk level.
categories.analogy: Like having four elemental toolkits you can swap between.
categories.primaryFocus: Baseline spellcasting access without spell slots
inScope: Ray of Frost / Cone of Cold (Cold at 11)

categories.title: Twin Elemental Wrath
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 3
categories.description: Spend 1 Ki to infuse two unarmed strikes with elemental damage.
categories.details: Choose two elements from Fire (1d6), Cold (1d6), Lightning (1d6), or Acid (1d6). Each attuned strike deals its elemental damage on top of normal unarmed strike damage. Lasts until the end of your next turn. Can pick the same element twice for doubled damage on one type.
categories.analogy: Temporarily charging your fists with elemental energy before a combo.
inScope: Any two elements from the four schools
Stacks with unarmed strike damage dice
outOfScope: Does not work with weapon attacks
Does not stack with itself (re-cast replaces)

categories.title: Four Point Attack
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 11
categories.description: Spend 4 Ki for four guaranteed elemental strikes, one per element.
categories.details: Each of four unarmed strikes automatically hits and deals 1d6 of a different elemental damage (Fire, Cold, Lightning, Acid). Cannot miss. Each strike can target a different enemy within reach. This is the build's ultimate ability, consuming your entire Ki pool at most levels.
categories.analogy: A four-elemental combo that guarantees hits regardless of AC.
inScope: Each can target a different enemy
outOfScope: Cannot be used if you have fewer than 4 Ki

categories.title: Flowing Barrier
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 7
categories.description: Spend Ki to boost your Armor Class defensively.
categories.details: As a bonus action, spend 1 or more Ki points to gain +1 AC per Ki spent until the start of your next turn. At Monk 7, this provides crucial survivability against high-damage enemies. Combine with high Dexterity for AC 20+ temporarily.
categories.analogy: Hardening your body like a force field for one turn.
inScope: Scales with Ki invested (1 Ki = +1 AC)
Lasts until start of next turn
Stacks with Dexterity and monk AC
outOfScope: Does not stack with itself (re-cast replaces)
Not useful in turns where you need Ki for offense

categories.title: Elemental Mastery
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 15
categories.description: Elemental spells no longer consume Ki points to cast.
categories.details: At Monk 15, casting elemental spells from your attuned schools costs 0 Ki. You can still voluntarily spend Ki to cast them at a higher level. This transforms the build's resource economy, allowing free spell spam while reserving Ki for Twin Elemental Wrath and Four Point Attack.
categories.analogy: Your elemental magic becomes an infinite resource.
inScope: All elemental spells cast for 0 Ki base cost
Optional Ki spend for higher-level casting
Enables Conjure Flame spam in every fight
Ice Knife and Call Lightning become free utilities
outOfScope: Still limited by spell slot availability for multiclass

categories.title: Empty Body
categories.subtitle: Monk Level 14
categories.description: Spend 4 Ki to cast Mirror Image or Teleport at will.
categories.details: At Monk 14, spend 4 Ki to cast either Mirror Image (three illusory copies that absorb hits) or Teleport (instant movement to any visible location). These are monk abilities, not spell slots. Teleport is invaluable for repositioning, flanking, and escaping dangerous situations.
categories.analogy: Phasing in and out of reality to control the battlefield.
inScope: Refreshes on Short Rest with Ki
outOfScope: Cannot cast both in the same activation

categories.title: Fire Spells
categories.subtitle: Pyromancy
categories.description: Fire spells excel at sustained AoE damage and area denial.
categories.details: Conjure Flame is your primary fire spell — it creates a persistent damage zone that enemies walk through. Burning Hands is a close-range cone blast. At higher levels, Fireball and Wall of Fire become available through spell upgrades.
categories.analogy: Setting the battlefield on fire and watching enemies cook.
categories.primaryFocus: Area denial and sustained damage over time
inScope: Wall of Fire (4th level — line barrier)
outOfScope: Non-damaging fire spells like Produce Flame light

categories.title: Cold Spells
categories.subtitle: Cryomancy
categories.description: Cold spells provide control, slow effects, and burst damage.
categories.details: Ray of Frost is your cold cantrip with a built-in slow effect. Ice Knife is the signature cold spell — a two-part attack that pierces a target then explodes around them. Cone of Cold delivers massive frontal AoE at higher levels.
categories.analogy: Freezing enemies in place before shattering them.
categories.primaryFocus: Crowd control and burst AoE damage
inScope: Ice Knife (2nd level — pierce + AoE burst)
Cone of Cold (5th level — frontal devastation)
Cone of Cold with Twinned Spell for dual targets

categories.title: Lightning Spells
categories.subtitle: Electromancy
categories.description: Lightning spells chain between targets and push enemies back.
categories.details: Shocking Grasp is your lightning cantrip — it deals damage and prevents opportunity attacks. Call Lightning summons a cloud that strikes repeatedly. Chain Lightning jumps between multiple targets for efficient multi-kill potential.
categories.analogy: A storm calling down bolts that arc between enemies.
categories.primaryFocus: Multi-target chain damage and knockback control

categories.title: Acid Spells
categories.subtitle: Corrosion
categories.description: Acid spells bypass resistance and apply damage-over-time effects.
categories.details: Acid Splash is your acid cantrip and hits multiple targets simultaneously. Acid Arrow delivers a delayed burst with a damage-over-time component. Chromatic Orb can be rolled to deal acid damage and benefits from upcasting.
categories.analogy: Corrosive pools that dissolve armor and flesh alike.

props.title: Boss Encounter
props.intro: You face a massive elemental-resistant boss in a narrow chamber. Your party is low on healing. What's your strategy?

start.prompt: The boss has resistance to Fire and Cold. Your Ki pool is full (5 Ki). What's your opening move?

choices.text: All-in with Four Point Attack — four guaranteed elemental hits bypass resistance splitting
Cast Call Lightning — lightning damage ignores the boss's fire/cold resistance
Flowing Barrier first — survive the boss's opening barrage

outcome.verdict: Four Point Attack devastates the boss with four different elements. Even with two resistances, Lightning and Acid hit full damage.
outcome.lesson: Four Point Attack's strength is resistance coverage. Four elements mean at most two are resisted.

outcome.verdict: Call Lightning deals solid lightning damage, but you spent Ki and your action. The boss closes distance and hits your party hard.
outcome.lesson: Single-element spells are predictable. Bosses often resist one or two elements, making single-element focus risky.

outcome.verdict: Flowing Barrier absorbs the boss's attacks, but you lost a turn dealing damage. The fight drags on longer.
outcome.lesson: Defense-first is safe but passive. Four Element Monk excels at overwhelming damage — use it.

choices.text: Close-range martial combat with elemental strikes
choices.rationale: Pure Monk path maximizes Ki and martial features.

level-choice.prompt: What act are you planning for?

choices.rationale: Early game needs survivability and consistent damage.
Late game unlocks Four Point Attack and legendary gear.

multiclass-path.prompt: How deep should the Sorcerer dip go?

leaf.recommendation: Pure Monk 6-8, focus on Twin Elemental Wrath + Conjure Flame.
leaf.explanation: Early game, Ki is limited. Twin Elemental Wrath (1 Ki) + Conjure Flame zone damage creates excellent sustained pressure. Prioritize Dexterity for AC and hit rate. Grab Patient-0 gauntlets in Act 2.
tradeoffs: Limited Ki means careful spending every fight
No Four Point Attack until Monk 11
Conjure Flame is your primary AoE tool

leaf.recommendation: Monk 12-13 pure, leverage Four Point Attack and legendary gear.
leaf.explanation: At Monk 12-13, you have 5 Ki, Four Point Attack, and access to both Patient-0 and Strix Cove Monk Cloak. Save 4 Ki for Four Point Attack on bosses, use Twin Elemental Wrath for clears. At Monk 15, Elemental Mastery makes spells free.
tradeoffs: Four Point Attack consumes most of your Ki
Strix Cove Cloak enables exploration utility

leaf.recommendation: Monk 10/Sorcerer 2 with Twinned Spell + Quickened Spell.
leaf.explanation: Twinned Spell doubles Ice Knife and Conjure Flame targets. Quickened Spell lets you cast a cantrip and make unarmed strikes in the same turn. The 2-level dip is the optimal investment — you get metamagic without sacrificing too much monk progression.
tradeoffs: Delayed Four Point Attack by 2 levels
Fewer Ki points than pure monk at same total level
Metamagic uses are limited per Short Rest

leaf.explanation: Deeper Sorcerer dip grants 3rd level spells like Fireball and Call Lightning, plus more metamagic points. You sacrifice monk features like Four Point Attack for broader spellcasting. Best for players who prefer spell diversity over martial abilities.
tradeoffs: Never reaches Four Point Attack or Empty Body
Reduced Ki pool limits monk abilities
Broader spell access compensates for lost martial features
